Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Acme Corp (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Jennifer - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated for Acme: 

Summary of what we heard
- Workload: multi-tenant customer support + real-time summarization for internal ops.
- Typical prompt: 150 tokens in, ~250 tokens out on average (400 tokens total per request).
- Expected volume: 120M tokens/month initially, scaling to ~600M tokens/month over 12 months.
- Peak QPS: 18 concurrent requests during peak windows; average requests per second ~10 (avg token arrival ~4000 tokens/sec at 120M/mo).
- Latency target: 95th <= 250ms for chat-style generation.
- Security: VPC + SOC2 required (we discussed Private/Dedicated options).

Pricing & budget context you shared
- Budget range: $6k - $10k/month committed (you noted procurement will consider higher for firm SLA/commits).
- Target unit economics: Acme is aiming for ~$50 - $80 per 1M tokens consumed (target $/1M tokens).

Questions / open items for Redwood sizing
1) Preferred GPU family: you mentioned interest in H100 for latency, but open to A100 if it materially reduces cost. Confirm preference.
2) Average sequence length distribution: do you have P95 or max sequence lengths? We used 1k tokens max for initial sizing.
3) Burst tolerance: are occasional bursts +2x expected and acceptable to be handled by short-term burst capacity?

Next steps
- I'll work with Marcus and Rishi to put together a 2-option Dedicated proposal: (A) H100 8-GPU pool (lower latency, higher unit cost), (B) A100 8-GPU pool (lower cost, slightly higher latency).
- We'll include estimated throughput (tokens/sec), expected $/1M tokens based on your volumes, and requested commitment levels.
- Schedule 30-min follow-up next week to review options and align on procurement timeline.

Attachments: draft estimate + baseline terms (attached).

Thanks - talk soon,
Marissa

Marissa - see initial sizing below (quick back-of-envelope). I attached a formal estimate spreadsheet.

Assumptions used:
- Model: redwood-13B-chat quantized equivalent; throughput and token costs anchored to H100/A100 benchmarks.
- Avg tokens per req: 400; p95 seq ~1,200 used for latency headroom.
- Sustained utilization target: 60-70% of reserved capacity to allow for burst traffic and maintenance windows.

Option A - H100 (8x H100-80GB)
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~6,000 tokens/sec (sustained), burstable to ~12k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Monthly capacity (at 70% util): ~11.5B tokens/month (ample headroom for 250M/mo).
- Estimated cost to Redwood (infrastructure + ops + licensing): equivalent to $700 - $900 per GPU per month (pro-forma) - internal figure for pricing only.
- Recommended list price to Acme (committed 12-mo): $12,500/mo for 8-GPU pool (includes burst buffer & 99.9% uptime SLA).
- Implied unit economics: at 250M tokens/mo, $12,500 / 250 = $50 / 1M tokens. At 120M tokens, implied $104 / 1M tokens.

Option B - A100 (8x A100-80GB)
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~4,000 tokens/sec (sustained), burstable to ~8k tokens/sec.
- Monthly capacity (70% util): ~7.6B tokens/month.
- Recommended list price (committed 12-mo): $9,000/mo for 8-GPU pool.
- Implied unit economics: at 250M tokens/mo, $9,000 / 250 = $36 / 1M tokens. At 120M tokens, $9,000 / 120 = $75 / 1M tokens.

4-GPU reserved options (H100 / A100) - for smaller footprint or staging
- H100 4x: $7,000/mo (implied ~$56 / 1M at 120M)
- A100 4x: $5,250/mo (implied ~$44 / 1M at 120M)

Notes / tradeoffs:
- H100 gives better p95 latency and more headroom for long sequences (p95 250ms target more achievable).
- A100 reduces committed monthly spend materially but may increase p95 latency by ~30-50ms depending on batch sizing; might require more aggressive batching tuning.
- We should include an add-on for burst capacity (hourly on-demand) if Acme expects >2x spikes; this could be priced on usage.

I've attached acme-dedicated-estimate.xlsx with line-item breakdowns (instance costs, ops fee, SLA uplift). LMK if you want different commitment tiers (6 vs 12 vs 24 mo) included.

- Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
